name: L3–L4 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Lumbar midline (primary); Lumbar paraspinal (common); Anterior thigh (common); Lateral thigh (spillover); Groin / inguinal (spillover)
clinical_note: Midline low back pain with anterior/lateral thigh referral. Discography localises the level poorly — overlap between adjacent levels is the norm.
source: Vanharanta / Ohnmeiss provocation discography series; Carragee et al., Spine 2000 (false-positive rates); DePalma et al., PM&R 2011 (midline vs paramidline).

name: L4–L5 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Lumbar midline (primary); Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Upper buttock (common); Posterior thigh (common); Lateral thigh (common); Lateral leg (spillover)
clinical_note: Midline low back pain, buttock and posterolateral leg. DePalma 2011: midline pain was present in 95.8% of confirmed discogenic cases versus 15.4% of facet and 12.9% of SI joint cases — the one location finding with real discriminating value.
differentiate_from: L5 radiculopathy; lumbar facet (but midline location favours disc)
source: Vanharanta / Ohnmeiss provocation discography series; Carragee et al., Spine 2000 (false-positive rates); DePalma et al., PM&R 2011 (midline vs paramidline).

name: L5–S1 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Lumbar midline (primary); Upper buttock (primary); Posterior thigh (common); Posterior calf (common); Lumbar paraspinal (common); Lateral leg (spillover); Sacroiliac joint region (spillover)
clinical_note: Midline low back, buttock, posterior thigh and calf. Pain extending below the knee correlates with the grade of annular disruption, not with which level is symptomatic.
source: Vanharanta / Ohnmeiss provocation discography series; Carragee et al., Spine 2000 (false-positive rates); DePalma et al., PM&R 2011 (midline vs paramidline).

name: L1–L2 facet joint
referral_zones: Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Flank / lateral trunk (primary); Iliac crest (common); Thoracolumbar junction (common); Greater trochanter / lateral hip (spillover)
clinical_note: Upper lumbar facets refer laterally and proximally — flank, iliac crest and lateral hip — rather than down the leg. McCall's volunteer data put the upper levels in the flank and greater trochanter region.
source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.

name: L2–L3 facet joint
referral_zones: Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Iliac crest (primary); Flank / lateral trunk (common); Greater trochanter / lateral hip (common); Upper buttock (spillover)
clinical_note: Lumbar paraspinal with lateral spread to the iliac crest and trochanter. Level-specific maps overlap heavily — McCall's own conclusion was 'considerable overlap' between levels.
source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.

name: L3–L4 facet joint
referral_zones: Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Upper buttock (primary); Iliac crest (common); Greater trochanter / lateral hip (common); Lateral thigh (spillover); Groin / inguinal (spillover)
clinical_note: Lumbar paraspinal, iliac crest, upper buttock and greater trochanter, beginning to reach the lateral thigh.
source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.

name: L4–L5 facet joint
referral_zones: Upper buttock (primary); Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Greater trochanter / lateral hip (primary); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Posterior thigh (common); Lateral thigh (common); Sacroiliac joint region (spillover)
clinical_note: One of the two most commonly implicated levels. Buttock and trochanteric referral dominate; Marks (1989) attributed most buttock and trochanteric pain to L4–L5.
source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.

name: L5–S1 facet joint
referral_zones: Upper buttock (primary); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (primary); Posterior thigh (primary); Lumbar paraspinal (common); Sacroiliac joint region (common); Greater trochanter / lateral hip (common); Lateral thigh (spillover)
clinical_note: Buttock and posterior thigh. Whether facet pain can reach below the knee is genuinely contested: Mooney & Robertson saw whole-leg pain in 3 of 20, but that is now widely attributed to large-volume saline rupturing the capsule. Windsor's electrical stimulation — a more specific stimulus — produced smaller, more proximal zones.
differentiate_from: SI joint (indistinguishable by pain location alone — DePalma 2011); L5/S1 radiculopathy
source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.

name: Hip joint
referral_zones: Upper buttock (primary); Groin / inguinal (primary); Anterior thigh (primary); Lateral thigh (common); Anterior knee / patella (common); Greater trochanter / lateral hip (common); Medial thigh (common); Medial knee (spillover); Anterior shin (spillover)
clinical_note: Buttock 71% — more common than groin, which contradicts the classic teaching. Thigh 57%, groin 55%, distal to knee 22%, foot 6%, isolated knee 2%, lower lumbar spine 0%. Fourteen distinct referral patterns were identified: there is no single dominant hip pattern.
differentiate_from: L2–L4 radiculopathy; SI joint; greater trochanteric pain syndrome. In adolescents with knee pain, always examine the hip — SCFE presents as knee pain in ~15%.
source: Lesher et al., Pain Medicine 2008 — fluoroscopically-guided intra-articular injection with pre-injection pain mapping, N=51 symptomatic patients.

name: Knee joint (intra-articular)
referral_zones: Anterior knee / patella (primary); Medial knee (common); Lateral knee (common); Anterior thigh (spillover); Posterior calf (spillover); Posterior knee / popliteal fossa (spillover)
clinical_note: Largely local, with referral into the anterior thigh and proximal calf. Graded C because — unlike the hip and SI joint — no controlled provocation mapping study was found for the knee.
source: Clinical observation; no controlled volunteer referral-mapping study identified.

name: Sacroiliac joint
referral_zones: Sacroiliac joint region (primary); Upper buttock (primary); Lumbar paraspinal (common); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Posterior thigh (common); Groin / inguinal (spillover); Posterior calf (spillover)
clinical_note: Graded B, not A: only the zone SHAPE — a consistent 3 × 10 cm area immediately caudal to the PSIS — comes from asymptomatic volunteers. Every percentage below comes from a symptomatic patient series. Slipman: buttock 94%, lower lumbar 72%, lower extremity roughly a quarter to a half (secondary sources report 28% and 50% for the same dataset), groin 14%, upper lumbar 6%. So SI pain CAN go below the knee — 'it stays above the knee' is not a safe rule.
differentiate_from: L5–S1 facet (DePalma 2011: paramidline location cannot separate the two); lumbar disc
source: Zone geometry: Fortin et al., Spine 1994 Part I — 10 ASYMPTOMATIC volunteers (grade-A design). All quoted percentages: Slipman et al., Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2000 — 50 SYMPTOMATIC patients (68 joints; 18 bilateral, 32 unilateral), selected by a single positive intra-articular block.

name: Lumbar & sacral interspinous ligaments
referral_zones: Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Upper buttock (common); Flank / lateral trunk (common); Sacroiliac joint region (common); Posterior thigh (common); Iliac crest (spillover)
clinical_note: Deep, diffuse, segmentally-organised ache that does NOT follow dermatomes. Upper lumbar levels refer to flank and hip; lower lumbar and sacral levels refer into buttock and posterior thigh, approaching the knee in a minority. Foundational but small-N, non-blinded work.
source: Kellgren, Clin Sci 1939; Feinstein et al., JBJS 1954 (as conventionally reported — the level-specific zones could not be verified against the primary tables).

name: Abductor hallucis
referral_zones: Plantar heel (primary); Medial arch (primary); Medial malleolus (spillover)
clinical_note: Medial heel and medial plantar foot.
differentiate_from: Tarsal tunnel syndrome; medial-band plantar fasciitis
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Adductor longus / brevis
referral_zones: Groin / inguinal (primary); Medial thigh (primary); Pubic / adductor origin (common); Medial knee (common); Medial leg (spillover)
clinical_note: Deep groin and anteromedial thigh, running down the medial leg to just below the knee.
differentiate_from: Adductor strain; osteitis pubis; hip labral pathology
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Adductor magnus
referral_zones: Medial thigh (primary); Pubic / adductor origin (primary); Perineum / pelvic floor (common); Groin / inguinal (common); Medial knee (spillover)
clinical_note: Ischiocondylar portion refers along the posteromedial thigh to the knee; the proximal/pubic portion produces a deep intrapelvic ache that may be perceived intravaginally or intrarectally.
differentiate_from: Chronic pelvic pain syndromes; adductor strain
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Biceps femoris
referral_zones: Posterior thigh (primary); Posterior knee / popliteal fossa (primary); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (spillover); Posterior calf (spillover)
clinical_note: Posterior thigh into the posterior knee and lateral popliteal fossa.
differentiate_from: Hamstring strain; S1 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Extensor digitorum brevis
referral_zones: Dorsum of foot (primary); Anterior ankle (spillover)
clinical_note: Local dorsolateral midfoot pain.
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Extensor digitorum longus
referral_zones: Dorsum of foot (primary); Anterior shin (common); Lateral toes (common); Anterior ankle (common)
clinical_note: Dorsum of the foot and anterolateral shin, referring into the dorsal aspect of the middle toes.
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Fibularis (peroneus) longus / brevis
referral_zones: Lateral malleolus (primary); Lateral leg (primary); Dorsum of foot (common); Lateral toes (spillover)
clinical_note: Lateral malleolus and lateral ankle/foot; longus spills to the lateral foot dorsum, brevis to the lateral shin.
differentiate_from: Chronic lateral ankle instability; superficial fibular n. entrapment; L5/S1 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Flexor digitorum brevis
referral_zones: Plantar forefoot / metatarsal heads (primary); Plantar heel (common); Medial arch (spillover)
clinical_note: Plantar surface under metatarsal heads 2–4 and the central heel.
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Flexor digitorum longus
referral_zones: Plantar forefoot / metatarsal heads (primary); Posterior calf (common); Medial arch (spillover)
clinical_note: Plantar surface over metatarsal heads 2–5, with a deep calf ache.
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Foot interossei
referral_zones: Plantar forefoot / metatarsal heads (primary); Lateral toes (primary); Dorsum of foot (common)
clinical_note: Local pain in the corresponding toe and web space. Third and fourth web-space trigger points can mimic Morton's neuroma.
differentiate_from: Morton's neuroma; metatarsalgia; stress fracture
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Gastrocnemius
referral_zones: Posterior calf (primary); Medial arch (common); Posterior knee / popliteal fossa (common); Medial leg (common); Lateral leg (spillover)
clinical_note: Medial head refers to the medial calf and the instep/arch; lateral head to the posterior knee and lateral calf. Implicated in nocturnal calf cramps.
differentiate_from: DVT (EXCLUDE FIRST in an acutely swollen, warm calf); S1 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Gluteus maximus
referral_zones: Upper buttock (primary); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (primary); Coccyx (common); Sacrum (common); Posterior thigh (spillover)
clinical_note: Diffuse ache over the buttock mass. The medial-fibre trigger point near the coccyx mimics coccydynia. Rarely crosses the knee.
differentiate_from: Coccydynia; SI joint dysfunction
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Gluteus medius
referral_zones: Iliac crest (primary); Upper buttock (primary); Sacrum (common); Sacroiliac joint region (common); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Posterior thigh (common); Lumbar paraspinal (common)
clinical_note: Posterior iliac crest, sacrum and the whole buttock — the classic 'low back pain' muscle. Spillover into the posterior thigh and upper calf.
differentiate_from: SI joint dysfunction; lumbar facet; L5 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Gluteus minimus
referral_zones: Lower buttock / gluteal fold (primary); Lateral thigh (primary); Lateral leg (primary); Lateral malleolus (common); Upper buttock (common); Posterior thigh (common); Posterior calf (common); Lateral knee (common)
clinical_note: THE pseudo-sciatica pattern, and the most convincing non-radicular mimic in the whole atlas. Anterior fibres refer from the lateral buttock down the OUTSIDE of the leg as far as the ankle; posterior fibres run down the back of the buttock and thigh, stopping at the calf. Leg pain to the ankle with no dermatomal, myotomal or reflex change should raise this immediately.
differentiate_from: L5 or S1 radiculopathy — the discriminator is the ABSENCE of reflex, myotome and dermatome findings
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Gracilis
referral_zones: Medial thigh (primary); Medial knee (spillover)
clinical_note: A diffuse, superficial ache with an itching quality along the medial thigh — distinctively surface-level rather than deep, which separates it from adductor longus.
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Iliopsoas
referral_zones: Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Groin / inguinal (primary); Anterior thigh (common); Anterior hip (common); Lumbar midline (spillover)
clinical_note: A vertical band in the ipsilateral upper lumbar paraspinal region plus anterior groin, spilling into the anterior thigh to the knee. A frequently missed mimic of discogenic back pain.
differentiate_from: Discogenic low back pain; hip flexor strain; intra-articular hip pathology
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Levator ani / coccygeus
referral_zones: Coccyx (primary); Sacrum (primary); Perineum / pelvic floor (common); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common)
clinical_note: Coccyx and lower sacrum — the coccydynia pattern — with buttock referral and a sensation of rectal fullness.
differentiate_from: Coccydynia; levator ani syndrome; proctalgia fugax
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Obturator internus
referral_zones: Perineum / pelvic floor (primary); Coccyx (primary); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Posterior thigh (spillover); Sacrum (spillover)
clinical_note: Deep pelvic floor, coccyx and posterior vaginal or rectal wall, spilling into the perineum and posterior thigh.
differentiate_from: Pudendal neuralgia; levator ani syndrome
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Pectineus
referral_zones: Groin / inguinal (primary); Anterior hip (common); Medial thigh (spillover)
clinical_note: Sharply localised deep pain in the groin crease with minimal spillover.
differentiate_from: Hip labral tear; intra-articular hip pathology; femoroacetabular impingement
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Piriformis
referral_zones: Sacroiliac joint region (primary); Upper buttock (primary); Sacrum (common); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Posterior thigh (common)
clinical_note: Over the SI joint, sacrum, buttock and posterior hip, extending into the proximal two-thirds of the posterior thigh. Distinguish the myofascial referral (rarely past the knee) from true piriformis syndrome — sciatic nerve entrapment — which does produce symptoms to the foot.
differentiate_from: Deep gluteal syndrome (true nerve entrapment); SI joint; S1 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Popliteus
referral_zones: Posterior knee / popliteal fossa (primary); Posterior calf (spillover)
clinical_note: Localised posterior knee pain, worse descending stairs or hills and with squatting. Minimal spillover.
differentiate_from: Popliteus tendinopathy; posterior horn meniscal tear; Baker's cyst
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Quadratus lumborum
referral_zones: Iliac crest (primary); Sacroiliac joint region (primary); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Greater trochanter / lateral hip (common); Groin / inguinal (common); Flank / lateral trunk (common); Lumbar paraspinal (common); Lower abdomen (spillover)
clinical_note: Superficial layer refers along the iliac crest and into the lower buttock and greater trochanter; deep layer concentrates over the SI joint, with spillover to the groin and lower lateral abdomen. One of the most consistently missed sources of 'SI joint' pain.
differentiate_from: SI joint dysfunction; greater trochanteric pain syndrome; hip pathology
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Quadratus plantae
referral_zones: Plantar heel (primary)
clinical_note: Central plantar heel pad. Distinctively, it mimics plantar fasciitis WITHOUT arch involvement — that absence is the discriminator.
differentiate_from: Plantar fasciitis (but without arch pain); Baxter's neuropathy
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Rectus abdominis (lower fibres)
referral_zones: Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Lower abdomen (primary); Sacrum (common); Sacroiliac joint region (spillover)
clinical_note: Refers as a band across the LOW BACK bilaterally, plus sacral and pelvic pain — easily missed because the examination focuses on posterior structures.
differentiate_from: Mechanical low back pain; visceral/gynaecological pathology (exclude first)
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Rectus femoris
referral_zones: Anterior knee / patella (primary); Anterior thigh (primary); Anterior hip (spillover)
clinical_note: Deep anterior thigh and, characteristically, the ANTERIOR KNEE — the referral is felt distally even though the trigger point sits proximally near the ASIS.
differentiate_from: Patellofemoral pain syndrome
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Sartorius
referral_zones: Anterior thigh (primary); Lateral thigh (common); Medial knee (common); Anterior hip (spillover)
clinical_note: Superficial, TINGLING or paraesthetic in quality — atypical for myofascial pain — running along the muscle from the anterolateral thigh toward the medial knee. The proximal trigger point near the ASIS can mimic meralgia paraesthetica.
differentiate_from: Meralgia paraesthetica (lateral femoral cutaneous n.)
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Semitendinosus / semimembranosus
referral_zones: Lower buttock / gluteal fold (primary); Posterior thigh (primary); Posterior knee / popliteal fossa (common); Medial knee (spillover)
clinical_note: Lower buttock crease and posteromedial thigh down to the popliteal fossa — a distinct laterality from biceps femoris.
differentiate_from: Proximal hamstring tendinopathy; ischiogluteal bursitis
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Soleus
referral_zones: Plantar heel (primary); Achilles region (primary); Posterior calf (common); Sacroiliac joint region (common); Posterior knee / popliteal fossa (spillover)
clinical_note: The LOWER trigger point near the Achilles refers to the HEEL and plantar surface — a textbook mimic of plantar fasciitis, reproducing weight-bearing heel pain. The upper/lateral trigger point refers, unexpectedly, to the SI JOINT region.
differentiate_from: Plantar fasciitis; Achilles tendinopathy; Baxter's neuropathy; SI joint dysfunction
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Tensor fasciae latae
referral_zones: Greater trochanter / lateral hip (primary); Lateral thigh (primary); Anterior hip (common); Lateral knee (spillover)
clinical_note: Anterolateral hip over the greater trochanter and down the lateral thigh along the IT band toward the lateral knee.
differentiate_from: Greater trochanteric pain syndrome; IT band syndrome
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Tibialis anterior
referral_zones: Anterior shin (primary); Anterior ankle (primary); Great toe / first web space (primary); Dorsum of foot (common)
clinical_note: Anterior ankle and the dorsum of the great toe and first ray, with local anterior shin pain.
differentiate_from: L5 radiculopathy; deep fibular n. entrapment; anterior compartment syndrome
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Tibialis posterior
referral_zones: Achilles region (primary); Plantar forefoot / metatarsal heads (primary); Medial arch (primary); Posterior calf (common); Plantar heel (common)
clinical_note: Diffuse — Achilles region, the ENTIRE plantar sole, and the posterior calf. The widest plantar distribution of any leg muscle.
differentiate_from: Tarsal tunnel syndrome; tibialis posterior tendinopathy; plantar fasciitis
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Vastus intermedius
referral_zones: Anterior thigh (primary); Anterior knee / patella (common)
clinical_note: Diffuse, poorly localised mid-anterior thigh spreading toward the anterior knee. Often underappreciated in 'unexplained' anterior thigh ache.
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Vastus lateralis
referral_zones: Lateral thigh (primary); Lateral knee (primary); Greater trochanter / lateral hip (common); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (spillover)
clinical_note: The widest referral of the quadriceps group — the entire lateral thigh from hip to knee, with the most distal trigger point referring to the lateral knee and proximal ones to the lateral hip and buttock.
differentiate_from: IT band syndrome; lateral knee pain; greater trochanteric pain syndrome
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: Vastus medialis
referral_zones: Medial knee (primary); Anterior knee / patella (common); Anterior thigh (spillover)
clinical_note: Medial knee, with the superior (VMO) trigger point referring deep into the knee joint. Classically associated with a reflex-inhibition 'buckling' or giving-way sensation in the ABSENCE of true ligamentous laxity.
differentiate_from: Meniscal tear; ACL insufficiency (but ligament tests are negative); patellofemoral pain
source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).

name: L3 nerve root
referral_zones: Anterior thigh (primary); Medial knee (common); Groin / inguinal (common); Medial thigh (common); Lumbar paraspinal (spillover)
clinical_note: Anterior and distal thigh to the medial knee. Prone knee bend is the loading test — 70% sensitive and 88% specific for L3 specifically.
source: Clinical radiculopathy series; ASIA sensory points; Suri et al. 2011 (femoral stretch test).

name: L4 nerve root
referral_zones: Medial leg (primary); Medial malleolus (primary); Medial knee (common); Anterior thigh (common); Lumbar paraspinal (spillover); Anterior shin (spillover)
clinical_note: Medial leg and medial malleolus, with anterior thigh involvement. The transitional root — it feeds both the femoral nerve and the lumbosacral trunk, so it can present like an upper or a lower lumbar lesion.
source: Clinical radiculopathy series; ASIA sensory points.

name: L5 nerve root
referral_zones: Lateral leg (primary); Dorsum of foot (primary); Great toe / first web space (primary); Posterior thigh (common); Upper buttock (common); Anterior shin (common); Lateral thigh (common); Lumbar paraspinal (spillover)
clinical_note: Lateral leg, dorsum of foot, great toe and first web space, with buttock and posterolateral thigh referral proximally. The commonest lumbar radiculopathy alongside S1.
differentiate_from: Common fibular n. at the fibular neck (spares hip abduction and inversion); gluteus minimus TrP
source: Clinical radiculopathy series; ASIA sensory points; SLR/slump literature.

name: S1 nerve root
referral_zones: Posterior calf (primary); Lateral malleolus (primary); Posterior thigh (primary); Lateral toes (common); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Plantar heel (common); Upper buttock (common)
clinical_note: Posterior thigh and calf into the lateral foot and lateral malleolus. Achilles reflex loss is the localising sign.
differentiate_from: Piriformis / deep gluteal syndrome; SI joint; hamstring pathology
source: Clinical radiculopathy series; ASIA sensory points.

name: C2–C3 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Occiput (primary); Upper posterior neck (primary); Suboccipital (common); Temporal / side of head (common); Vertex / top of head (common); Face / cheek / jaw (spillover)
clinical_note: Head pain is disproportionately a C2–3 phenomenon: 19/40 reported head pain (occipital most common, then temporal, then parietal) and 4 patients had EXCLUSIVELY head pain with no neck component. 80% of painful C2–3 discs looked normal on MRI.
source: Schellhas et al., AJNR 2000 — provocation discography, 40 chronic head/neck pain patients; Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (41 subjects, 101 maps).

name: C3–C4 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Mid posterior neck (primary); Upper posterior neck (common); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common); Suboccipital (spillover); Anterior neck / throat (spillover); Face / cheek / jaw (spillover); Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (spillover)
clinical_note: Neck, subocciput, trapezius, anterior neck, face, shoulder, interscapular and limb — one of the broadest referral fields of any cervical disc.
source: Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (19 maps); Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000.

name: C4–C5 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Lower posterior neck (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (primary); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common); Superior angle of scapula (common); Anterior chest / precordial / breast (spillover); Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (spillover); Anterior / lateral upper arm (spillover)
clinical_note: Neck, shoulder, interscapular, trapezius, extremity, face, chest, subocciput. Grubb & Kelly found anterior chest wall referral begins at this level.
source: Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (27 maps); Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000.

name: C5–C6 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Lower posterior neck (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (primary); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common); Anterior chest / precordial / breast (common); Superior angle of scapula (common); Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (spillover); Anterior / lateral upper arm (spillover)
clinical_note: Neck, trapezius, interscapular, subocciput, anterior neck, chest, face. Bilateral pain occurred in 30–62% of discs at every level — laterality of pain does NOT indicate laterality of pathology.
source: Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (27 maps); Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000.

name: C6–C7 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (primary); Lower posterior neck (common); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Vertebral border of scapula (common); Anterior / lateral upper arm (spillover); Dorsoradial forearm (spillover); Anterior chest / precordial / breast (spillover)
clinical_note: Neck, interscapular, trapezius, shoulder, extremity, subocciput. Arm referral is most consistent at this level and C5–6.
source: Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (16 maps); Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000.

name: C7–T1 intervertebral disc
referral_zones: Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (primary); Lower posterior neck (common); Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (common)
clinical_note: Mid-posterior neck through to the mid-thoracic spine, and the interscapular region. Very few mapped cases — the weakest-supported of the cervical disc levels.
source: Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000; Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (only 2 maps at this level).

name: C0–C1 atlanto-occipital joint
referral_zones: Suboccipital (primary); Occiput (common); Upper posterior neck (common); Vertex / top of head (spillover); Frontal / supraorbital / retro-orbital (spillover)
clinical_note: Consistently suboccipital; may extend cephalad toward the vertex and occasionally the frontal region. Very small volunteer sample (N=5) — treat the zone as indicative, not precise.
source: Dreyfuss, Michaelsen & Fletcher, Spine 1994 — provocative intra-articular injection, 5 asymptomatic volunteers.

name: C1–C2 lateral atlanto-axial joint
referral_zones: Occiput (primary); Suboccipital (primary); Ear / retromastoid (common); Upper posterior neck (common)
clinical_note: Discrete unilateral pain at the occipito-cervical junction, retromastoid area and upper cervical region. Aprill's clinical criteria (occipital pain + focal C1 transverse process tenderness + restricted rotation) had only 60% positive predictive value — distribution alone cannot substitute for a diagnostic block.
source: Dreyfuss et al., Spine 1994 (N=5 volunteers); clinical validation by controlled blocks — Aprill, Axinn & Bogduk, Cephalalgia 2002 (21/34 patients confirmed).

name: C2–C3 facet joint (third occipital nerve)
referral_zones: Upper posterior neck (primary); Occiput (primary); Suboccipital (common); Ear / retromastoid (common); Vertex / top of head (common); Frontal / supraorbital / retro-orbital (spillover); Temporal / side of head (spillover)
clinical_note: Upper neck pain extending into the head — toward the ear, vertex, forehead or eye. The most common source of headache after whiplash: third occipital nerve headache found in 27% of whiplash patients overall and 53% of those whose dominant complaint was headache.
differentiate_from: Cervicogenic headache from C1–2; occipital neuralgia; migraine
source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; validated clinically in Aprill et al. 1990; Lord et al., JNNP 1994 — controlled double-blind blocks.

name: C3–C4 facet joint
referral_zones: Upper posterior neck (primary); Mid posterior neck (primary); Lower posterior neck (common); Occiput (common); Suboccipital (spillover)
clinical_note: Neck pain from the suboccipital region down to the lower neck — characteristically WITHOUT shoulder involvement. That absence is the useful discriminator from C4–5 and below.
source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; corroborated in symptomatic patients by Fukui et al., Pain 1996.

name: C4–C5 facet joint
referral_zones: Lower posterior neck (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (primary); Mid posterior neck (common); Superior angle of scapula (spillover)
clinical_note: More caudally located than C3–4: top of the shoulder and the lower part of the neck. Fukui found lower posterior cervical in 76% and suprascapular in 43% of symptomatic patients.
source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; Fukui et al., Pain 1996.

name: C5–C6 facet joint
referral_zones: Lower posterior neck (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (primary); Superior angle of scapula (common); Posterior deltoid / posterior shoulder (spillover); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (spillover)
clinical_note: Lower neck, top of the scapula and the shoulder region above the level of the scapular spine. Together with C2–3, one of the two most frequently implicated levels in chronic neck pain (~35% of cases).
source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; Fukui et al., Pain 1996; prevalence data from Cooper, Bailey & Bogduk, Pain Medicine 2007.

name: C6–C7 facet joint
referral_zones: Superior angle of scapula (primary); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (primary); Lower posterior neck (common); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Vertebral border of scapula (spillover)
clinical_note: Extends caudally as far as the scapular spine. Fukui: superior scapular angle 48%, mid-scapular 41%, lower posterior cervical 33%.
source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; Fukui et al., Pain 1996.

name: C7–T1 facet joint
referral_zones: Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (primary); Vertebral border of scapula (common); Superior angle of scapula (common); Lower posterior neck (spillover)
clinical_note: Mid-scapular region in 86% of patients; superior angle of scapula in 28%. Note this level rests on patient-provocation data only — a tier below the C2–3 to C6–7 volunteer maps.
source: Fukui et al., Pain 1996 — intra-articular contrast/dorsal ramus stimulation in 61 SYMPTOMATIC patients. Not covered by the Dwyer volunteer study.

name: Lower thoracic facet joints (T9–T12)
referral_zones: Thoracolumbar junction (primary); Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (common); Flank / lateral trunk (common); Lumbar paraspinal (spillover); Lumbar midline (spillover)
clinical_note: Paraspinal pain at and just below the segment, with modest lateral spread into the flank. Graded B rather than A because the range is split: T9–10 and T10–11 have volunteer-provocation evidence, but T11–12 rests on symptomatic-patient data alone. Same caveat as the rest of the thoracic spine: granular per-segment diagrams circulating in handouts are illustrative composites, not something either primary study reports.
source: Dreyfuss et al., Spine 1994 — volunteers, but only as far down as T10–11; Fukui et al., Reg Anesth 1997 — T11–12, symptomatic patients only.

name: Mid thoracic facet joints (T5–T8)
referral_zones: Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (primary); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common); Flank / lateral trunk (spillover)
clinical_note: Local paraspinal zone lateral to the joint, half a segment above to one segment below. IMPORTANT: 27% of injected joints produced no pain at all, and the resulting patterns overlap heavily with costotransverse joint and soft-tissue patterns — thoracic maps are far less segment-discriminating than the cervical ones.
source: Dreyfuss, Tibiletti & Dreyer, Spine 1994 — distension in asymptomatic volunteers (T3–4 to T10–11).

name: Upper thoracic facet joints (T1–T4)
referral_zones: Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (primary); Vertebral border of scapula (common); Superior angle of scapula (spillover); Lower posterior neck (spillover)
clinical_note: Local paraspinal pain lateral to the joint, from about half a segment above to a full segment below the joint of origin. Does not cross the midline and does not reliably distinguish adjacent levels.
source: Fukui et al., Reg Anesth 1997 (symptomatic patients, T1–2/T2–3); Dreyfuss, Tibiletti & Dreyer, Spine 1994 (volunteers, from T3–4 down).

name: Acromioclavicular joint
referral_zones: Top of shoulder / suprascapular (primary); Superior angle of scapula (common); Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (common); Lower posterior neck (spillover); Lateral deltoid / lateral shoulder (spillover)
clinical_note: Burning pain over the joint itself, deep in the supraspinatus fossa and upper trapezius, sometimes extending to the anterolateral deltoid and anterolateral neck. Can convincingly mimic cervical or trapezius myofascial pain.
differentiate_from: Upper trapezius myofascial pain; C4–5/C5–6 facet; cervical radiculopathy
source: Gerber, Galantay & Hersche, JSES 1998 — hypertonic saline injection mapping in asymptomatic volunteers. (Sample size not verifiable from open sources.)

name: Subacromial space / bursa
referral_zones: Lateral deltoid / lateral shoulder (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Anterior / lateral upper arm (spillover)
clinical_note: Intense pain at the lateral border of the acromion and over the lateral deltoid — a more focal and more distal pattern than AC joint referral. This is the classic 'impingement' distribution.
differentiate_from: C5 radiculopathy; supraspinatus/infraspinatus myofascial referral; axillary nerve entrapment
source: Gerber, Galantay & Hersche, JSES 1998 — hypertonic saline injection in asymptomatic volunteers.

name: Cervical interspinous ligaments
referral_zones: Mid posterior neck (primary); Lower posterior neck (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common); Occiput (spillover)
clinical_note: Deep, diffuse, segmentally-organised ache in the neck and shoulder girdle that does NOT follow dermatomes. Foundational but small-N, non-blinded 1930s–50s work; Inman & Saunders noted the resulting maps 'could not be given with any great precision'.
source: Kellgren, Clin Sci 1939 — hypertonic saline injection in volunteers; replicated in principle by Feinstein et al. 1954.

name: Thoracic interspinous ligaments
referral_zones: Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (primary); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common); Thoracolumbar junction (common); Flank / lateral trunk (common); Lateral chest wall / axillary line (spillover)
clinical_note: Segmental paraspinal ache with lateral spread around the chest wall. Superficial structures (supraspinous ligament, spinous process) give sharply localised pain instead — the depth of the structure, not its level, determines whether pain refers.
source: Kellgren, Clin Sci 1939; Feinstein et al. 1954.

name: Adductor pollicis
referral_zones: Thumb / thenar eminence (primary); Thumb–index web space (primary); Palm (common); Wrist (common)
clinical_note: Base of the thumb, thumb–index web space, centre of the palm and the wrist. Confined to the hand — can convincingly mimic carpal tunnel syndrome.
differentiate_from: Carpal tunnel syndrome; CMC arthritis
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Biceps brachii
referral_zones: Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (primary); Anterior / lateral upper arm (primary); Antecubital / anterior elbow (common); Volar forearm (spillover)
clinical_note: Anterior shoulder (front of deltoid) and down the front of the arm to the antecubital crease.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Brachialis
referral_zones: Antecubital / anterior elbow (primary); Thumb / thenar eminence (primary); Thumb–index web space (primary); Anterior / lateral upper arm (common)
clinical_note: Front of the elbow over the muscle belly, with a distinctive projection to the base and dorsal web space of the THUMB — that thumb referral is the signature.
differentiate_from: C6 radiculopathy; de Quervain's; CMC arthritis
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Brachioradialis
referral_zones: Lateral epicondyle / lateral elbow (primary); Dorsoradial forearm (primary); Thumb–index web space (primary); Thumb / thenar eminence (common); Wrist (spillover)
clinical_note: Lateral epicondyle ('tennis elbow' mimic) and down the dorsoradial forearm to the web space between thumb and index finger.
differentiate_from: Lateral epicondylalgia; radial tunnel syndrome; C6 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Coracobrachialis
referral_zones: Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (primary); Anterior / lateral upper arm (common); Posterior upper arm (common); Dorsal forearm (common); Dorsum of hand (common)
clinical_note: Anterior deltoid and front of the upper arm, with an unusually long reach for a small muscle — down the entire posterior arm to the dorsal forearm and hand.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Deltoid (anterior / posterior)
referral_zones: Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (primary); Posterior deltoid / posterior shoulder (primary); Lateral deltoid / lateral shoulder (common); Anterior / lateral upper arm (spillover); Posterior upper arm (spillover)
clinical_note: Localised to the involved third of the muscle itself, spreading only into the adjacent upper arm. Unusual among shoulder muscles for NOT projecting distal to the elbow.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: External / internal obliques
referral_zones: Epigastric / upper abdomen (primary); Groin / inguinal (primary); Anterior hip (primary); Pubic / adductor origin (primary); Lower abdomen (common); Flank / lateral trunk (common); Lateral chest wall / axillary line (spillover)
clinical_note: Upper fibres refer to the epigastrium and mimic heartburn; lower fibres refer to the groin and, in men, the testicle/scrotum. A well-known McBurney's-point mimic on the right — sometimes mistaken for appendicitis.
differentiate_from: Appendicitis (EXCLUDE FIRST); inguinal hernia; hip pathology
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Finger extensors (EDC / EIP)
referral_zones: Dorsal forearm (primary); Dorsum of hand (primary); Wrist (common); Radial digits (index, middle) (common); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (common)
clinical_note: Dorsal forearm and wrist referring into the dorsum of the corresponding finger(s) — a roughly segmental, one-slip-per-finger pattern.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: First dorsal interosseous
referral_zones: Radial digits (index, middle) (primary); Thumb–index web space (primary); Dorsum of hand (common)
clinical_note: Radial side of the index finger, running its full length to the fingertip, plus the dorsal web space. Frequently mistaken for digital nerve entrapment.
differentiate_from: Digital nerve entrapment; C6/C7 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Iliocostalis lumborum
referral_zones: Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Lumbar midline (primary); Sacroiliac joint region (common); Upper buttock (common); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Flank / lateral trunk (common); Thoracolumbar junction (common)
clinical_note: Local low back extending into the buttock; sits more lateral than the longissimus pattern.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Iliocostalis thoracis
referral_zones: Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (primary); Flank / lateral trunk (common); Lateral chest wall / axillary line (common); Anterior chest / precordial / breast (common); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common)
clinical_note: Segmental paraspinal band at the level of the trigger point that WRAPS AROUND THE CHEST WALL following the rib contours — can mimic cardiac or pleuritic pain.
differentiate_from: Cardiac / pleuritic pain (EXCLUDE FIRST); thoracic facet; costotransverse joint
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Infraspinatus
referral_zones: Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (primary); Lateral deltoid / lateral shoulder (common); Anterior / lateral upper arm (common); Dorsoradial forearm (common); Vertebral border of scapula (common); Radial digits (index, middle) (spillover); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (spillover)
clinical_note: Deep ache in the ANTERIOR shoulder/deltoid — the single most classic 'shoulder pain' myofascial pattern. Spillover down the lateral arm and radial forearm, plus local pain at the vertebral border of the scapula. Characteristically painful at rest and prevents sleeping on the affected side. The experimental corroboration covers only the arm component, not the anterior-deltoid, forearm or scapular zones, so the grade stays C with the rest of the myofascial maps.
differentiate_from: C5 radiculopathy (has weakness/reflex change); subacromial bursitis (painful arc); AC joint
source: Zone map: Travell & Simons Vol. 1. Referral direction separately corroborated by hypertonic saline injection in healthy volunteers producing referred pain in the ipsilateral upper arm (Leffler et al., Eur J Pain 2000).

name: Latissimus dorsi
referral_zones: Inferior angle of scapula (primary); Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (common); Medial upper arm (common); Posterior upper arm (common); Medial epicondyle / medial elbow (common); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (common); Ulnar forearm (spillover)
clinical_note: Constant ache over the inferior angle of the scapula and mid-back (the 'cape' of pain), spilling down the medial/posterior arm to the medial epicondyle and into the ring and little fingers.
differentiate_from: C8 radiculopathy; cubital tunnel
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Levator scapulae
referral_zones: Lower posterior neck (primary); Vertebral border of scapula (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Superior angle of scapula (common); Posterior deltoid / posterior shoulder (spillover)
clinical_note: Angle of the neck (the neck–shoulder junction) and along the vertebral border of the scapula to its inferior angle. Classically limits cervical rotation toward the painful side.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Longissimus thoracis
referral_zones: Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (primary); Thoracolumbar junction (primary); Lumbar paraspinal (common); Lumbar midline (common); Sacroiliac joint region (common); Upper buttock (common); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (common); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (spillover)
clinical_note: Paraspinal band at the trigger point level — upper points stay local with some radiation toward the scapula; lower points extend into the buttock, generally more MEDIAL than the iliocostalis lumborum pattern.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Lower trapezius
referral_zones: Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common); Lower posterior neck (common); Occiput (spillover)
clinical_note: Local ache at the T6–T9 paraspinal origin and over the top of the shoulder, with spillover to the base of the neck and mastoid — Travell & Simons specifically flag this 'far' referral as atypical.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Middle trapezius
referral_zones: Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (primary); Vertebral border of scapula (common); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (spillover); Lower posterior neck (spillover)
clinical_note: Superficial burning ache between the vertebral border of the scapula and the spine, locally over C7–T3.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Multifidi
referral_zones: Lumbar paraspinal (primary); Lumbar midline (primary); Sacroiliac joint region (primary); Upper buttock (primary); Lower buttock / gluteal fold (primary); Mid posterior neck (common); Occiput (common); Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (common); Thoracolumbar junction (common)
clinical_note: Very localised deep segmental pain directly over or adjacent to the spinous process at the level involved. Cervical level refers to the occiput; lumbosacral level refers to the buttock and occasionally the posterior thigh, mimicking sciatica.
differentiate_from: Lumbar radiculopathy; facet joint pain
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Opponens pollicis
referral_zones: Thumb / thenar eminence (primary); Wrist (common); Thumb–index web space (spillover)
clinical_note: Runs the length of the palmar/radial thumb itself, occasionally to the dorsal thumb and volar wrist.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Pectoralis major
referral_zones: Anterior chest / precordial / breast (primary); Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (common); Medial upper arm (common); Medial epicondyle / medial elbow (common); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (common); Ulnar forearm (spillover)
clinical_note: Anterior chest wall and breast. Clinically important: sternal-head trigger points near the 5th–6th costal cartilage can produce precordial pain and arrhythmia-like sensations that mimic cardiac disease — a well-documented diagnostic pitfall. Spillover down the medial arm to the ulnar digits.
differentiate_from: Angina / cardiac pain (EXCLUDE FIRST); costochondritis; C8–T1 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Pectoralis minor
referral_zones: Anterior chest / precordial / breast (primary); Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (common); Medial upper arm (common); Ulnar forearm (common); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (common)
clinical_note: Anterior chest and shoulder below the clavicle, referring down the medial arm and forearm to the ulnar three digits — overlapping the ulnar/thoracic outlet pattern.
differentiate_from: Neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome (subcoracoid space); C8 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Pronator teres
referral_zones: Volar forearm (primary); Wrist (primary); Thumb / thenar eminence (common); Radial digits (index, middle) (common); Antecubital / anterior elbow (common); Palm (spillover)
clinical_note: Volar proximal forearm and radial wrist, spilling to the radial three digits and thenar region. Can accompany true median nerve paresthesia (pronator teres syndrome).
differentiate_from: Carpal tunnel syndrome; pronator syndrome; C6 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Rectus abdominis
referral_zones: Epigastric / upper abdomen (primary); Lower abdomen (primary); Thoracolumbar junction (common); Lumbar paraspinal (common); Lumbar midline (common); Mid thoracic paraspinal (T5–T8) (common); Anterior chest / precordial / breast (spillover)
clinical_note: Hallmark feature: upper trigger points refer BILATERALLY across the mid and low back and can mimic epigastric or cardiac pain; lower trigger points refer bilaterally to the low back and sacral region and can produce colicky abdominal pain with GI symptoms.
differentiate_from: Visceral pathology (EXCLUDE FIRST); lumbar facet; discogenic low back pain
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Rhomboid major / minor
referral_zones: Vertebral border of scapula (primary); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common)
clinical_note: Superficial, localised ache along the vertebral border of the scapula. One of the few patterns with essentially NO spillover and no projection into the arm — that confinement is the diagnostic clue.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Scalenes (anterior / middle / posterior)
referral_zones: Anterior chest / precordial / breast (primary); Vertebral border of scapula (primary); Dorsoradial forearm (primary); Thumb / thenar eminence (common); Radial digits (index, middle) (common); Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (common); Anterior / lateral upper arm (common); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common)
clinical_note: Anterior/pectoral chest wall, vertebral border of scapula, and down the radial forearm to thumb and index finger — closely mimics C6 radiculopathy. Posterior scalene skews more interscapular.
differentiate_from: C6 radiculopathy; neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome; carpal tunnel
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Serratus anterior
referral_zones: Lateral chest wall / axillary line (primary); Inferior angle of scapula (common); Medial upper arm (common); Ulnar forearm (spillover); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (spillover); Anterior chest / precordial / breast (spillover)
clinical_note: Lateral chest wall in the mid-axillary line — the classic 'stitch in the side' — wrapping to the inferior scapular angle and down the medial arm to the ulnar forearm and digits. Often accompanied by air hunger / difficulty taking a deep breath.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Serratus posterior inferior
referral_zones: Thoracolumbar junction (primary); Flank / lateral trunk (spillover)
clinical_note: Localised, persistent ache at the thoracolumbar junction over the muscle itself. One of the more confined trunk patterns — in sharp contrast to serratus posterior superior's long reach into the hand.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Serratus posterior superior
referral_zones: Vertebral border of scapula (primary); Inferior angle of scapula (common); Posterior deltoid / posterior shoulder (common); Posterior upper arm (common); Ulnar forearm (common); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (common); Dorsum of hand (spillover)
clinical_note: Deep, poorly localised ache UNDER the scapula, referring down the posterior arm to the ulnar forearm, hand and little finger, with occasional numbness in a C8–T1 distribution. The 'ache I can't reach'.
differentiate_from: C8 radiculopathy; neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Splenius capitis
referral_zones: Vertex / top of head (primary); Upper posterior neck (spillover)
clinical_note: A 'boring' pain focused at the very top of the head. Classically no frontal or ocular involvement — that absence distinguishes it from sternocleidomastoid.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Splenius cervicis
referral_zones: Frontal / supraorbital / retro-orbital (primary); Occiput (primary); Upper posterior neck (common); Lower posterior neck (common); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (spillover)
clinical_note: Retro-orbital pain (behind the eye) and the angle of the neck/occiput, with reported ipsilateral blurred vision as a concomitant.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Sternocleidomastoid (both heads)
referral_zones: Vertex / top of head (primary); Face / cheek / jaw (primary); Frontal / supraorbital / retro-orbital (primary); Ear / retromastoid (primary); Temporal / side of head (common); Anterior neck / throat (common); Anterior chest / precordial / breast (spillover)
clinical_note: Sternal head: vertex, cheek/malar region, supraorbital ridge, deep in the ear, pharynx (sore-throat sensation), sternum. Clavicular head: bilateral frontal headache, deep ear pain, plus autonomic phenomena (postural dizziness, disequilibrium, tinnitus, lacrimation) that are a hallmark feature.
differentiate_from: Trigeminal neuralgia; TMD; cervicogenic dizziness; sinus headache
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Suboccipital group
referral_zones: Suboccipital (primary); Occiput (primary); Temporal / side of head (common); Vertex / top of head (common); Frontal / supraorbital / retro-orbital (common)
clinical_note: Diffuse, deep, band- or 'halo'-like pain from the occiput over the top of the head toward the temple and eye. Travell & Simons note this pattern does not map to a crisp cutaneous zone.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Subscapularis
referral_zones: Posterior deltoid / posterior shoulder (primary); Inferior angle of scapula (common); Vertebral border of scapula (common); Posterior upper arm (common); Wrist (common)
clinical_note: Severe deep pain over the posterior shoulder and scapula — the 'shoulder holster' pattern — with a distinctive circumferential band around the wrist in severe cases. Strongly associated with frozen-shoulder-type restriction.
differentiate_from: Adhesive capsulitis; posterior labral pathology
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Supinator
referral_zones: Lateral epicondyle / lateral elbow (primary); Dorsoradial forearm (common); Thumb–index web space (common); Thumb / thenar eminence (spillover)
clinical_note: Lateral epicondyle and proximal dorsal forearm — mimics resistant lateral epicondylalgia and radial tunnel syndrome — with spillover to the dorsal thumb web space.
differentiate_from: Lateral epicondylalgia (resistant); PIN/radial tunnel entrapment
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Supraspinatus
referral_zones: Lateral deltoid / lateral shoulder (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Anterior / lateral upper arm (common); Lateral epicondyle / lateral elbow (common); Dorsoradial forearm (spillover); Wrist (spillover)
clinical_note: Deep, boring ache centred over the mid-deltoid, spilling down the arm and forearm, occasionally to the wrist.
differentiate_from: Subacromial impingement; C5 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Teres major
referral_zones: Posterior deltoid / posterior shoulder (primary); Inferior angle of scapula (common); Posterior upper arm (common); Olecranon / posterior elbow (spillover)
clinical_note: Posterior deltoid and the inferior angle of the scapula, spilling down the back of the arm toward the elbow.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Teres minor
referral_zones: Posterior deltoid / posterior shoulder (primary)
clinical_note: A small, circumscribed patch of deep ache over the posterior deltoid near the axillary scapular border. Notably does NOT radiate — the confinement is the clue.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Triceps brachii
referral_zones: Posterior upper arm (primary); Olecranon / posterior elbow (primary); Posterior deltoid / posterior shoulder (common); Dorsal forearm (common); Dorsum of hand (spillover); Lateral epicondyle / lateral elbow (spillover); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (spillover)
clinical_note: Posterior shoulder, posterior upper arm and the olecranon/posterior elbow, spilling down the posterior forearm to the dorsum of the hand.
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1 (multiple distinct trigger point sites).

name: Upper trapezius
referral_zones: Lower posterior neck (primary); Temporal / side of head (primary); Mid posterior neck (common); Face / cheek / jaw (common); Occiput (common); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Ear / retromastoid (spillover)
clinical_note: Posterolateral neck up to the temple — the classic unilateral 'tension headache' pattern — and the angle of the jaw. Spillover to occiput and mastoid. One of only two muscles here whose referral DIRECTION has independent experimental support; the grade stays C because the mapped zone borders still come from clinical observation, and the saline work corroborates direction, not extent.
differentiate_from: C2–3 facet; cervicogenic headache; migraine
source: Zone map: Travell & Simons Vol. 1 (clinical observation). Referral DIRECTION separately corroborated by controlled hypertonic saline injection in healthy volunteers (Graven-Nielsen, Arendt-Nielsen et al.).

name: Wrist / finger flexors (FCR, FCU, FDS, FDP)
referral_zones: Volar forearm (primary); Palm (primary); Ulnar forearm (common); Wrist (common); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (common); Radial digits (index, middle) (spillover)
clinical_note: Volar forearm referring to the palm, volar wrist and corresponding fingers — FCU skews ulnar/little finger, FCR skews radial palm. Palmaris longus is distinct: a superficial, hypersensitive 'pins-and-needles' patch in the centre of the palm rather than a deep ache.
differentiate_from: Carpal tunnel syndrome; Guyon's canal; C8 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: Wrist extensors (ECRL / ECRB / ECU)
referral_zones: Lateral epicondyle / lateral elbow (primary); Wrist (primary); Dorsal forearm (common); Dorsum of hand (common); Radial digits (index, middle) (spillover)
clinical_note: ECRL/ECRB: lateral epicondyle spilling to the dorsum of the hand and wrist (ECRB into the dorsal middle finger). ECU stays fairly localised to the dorsal-ulnar wrist.
differentiate_from: Lateral epicondylalgia; C6–C7 radiculopathy
source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.

name: C4 nerve root (dynatome)
referral_zones: Lower posterior neck (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (primary); Superior angle of scapula (spillover)
clinical_note: Base of neck and top of shoulder. Only 4 stimulations at this level — the least-supported root map.
source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 — fluoroscopically guided cervical nerve root stimulation, 134 stimulations in 87 subjects (only 4 at C4).

name: C5 nerve root (dynatome)
referral_zones: Lateral deltoid / lateral shoulder (primary); Top of shoulder / suprascapular (common); Anterior / lateral upper arm (common); Lower posterior neck (common); Anterior deltoid / anterior shoulder (spillover)
clinical_note: Lateral shoulder and lateral arm. NOTE: dynatomal (symptom) maps are measurably broader than textbook dermatomes — the expected pattern held in as little as 54% of stimulations.
source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 (14 stimulations at C5).

name: C6 nerve root (dynatome)
referral_zones: Dorsoradial forearm (primary); Thumb / thenar eminence (primary); Radial digits (index, middle) (common); Anterior / lateral upper arm (common); Lateral deltoid / lateral shoulder (common); Lower posterior neck (common); Ulnar digits (ring, little) (spillover); Superior angle of scapula (spillover)
clinical_note: Lateral arm, dorsoradial forearm, thumb and index finger — but ~30% of C6 stimulations also produced LITTLE FINGER symptoms, classically a C8 finding. Intrathecal anastomoses between adjacent dorsal roots (up to ~61%) blur segment-specific territories.
differentiate_from: C7 root; radial tunnel; de Quervain's; carpal tunnel
source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 (43 stimulations at C6).

name: C7 nerve root (dynatome)
referral_zones: Dorsal forearm (primary); Radial digits (index, middle) (primary); Posterior upper arm (common); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (common); Vertebral border of scapula (common); Dorsum of hand (common); Olecranon / posterior elbow (spillover)
clinical_note: Posterior arm, dorsal forearm, middle finger, and prominent interscapular/scapular referral. Proximal (scapular) referral is far more common in dynatomal maps than dermatome charts suggest.
source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 (52 stimulations at C7 — the largest subgroup).

name: C8 nerve root (dynatome)
referral_zones: Ulnar digits (ring, little) (primary); Ulnar forearm (primary); Medial upper arm (common); Medial epicondyle / medial elbow (common); Interscapular / upper thoracic paraspinal (spillover); Radial digits (index, middle) (spillover)
clinical_note: Ulnar forearm, ring and little fingers — but ~24% of C8 stimulations produced INDEX FINGER symptoms, classically a C6/C7 finding. Symptom location does not reliably localise the root.
differentiate_from: Cubital tunnel; Guyon's canal; neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome
source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 (21 stimulations at C8).
